en: The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Four Dharmas, translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlabhadra of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove.
At the Jetavana Grove, together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus, as well as an immeasurable multitude of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
the World-Honored One then addressed the bhikṣus:

"There are four dharmas that a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should constantly practice throughout their entire lifespan, and which must not be abandoned even if they encounter circumstances that threaten their life."
What are these four?
Monks and bodhisattvas must, for as long as they live—even at the cost of their own lives—never abandon the bodhicitta;
monks and bodhisattvas must, for as long as they live—even at the cost of their own lives—never abandon spiritual friends.
O bhikṣus and bodhisattvas, for as long as life lasts, even when encountering circumstances that threaten your lives, you must never abandon patient endurance and joyful delight;
O bhikṣus and bodhisattvas, for as long as life lasts, even when encountering circumstances that threaten your lives, you must by all means never abandon the forest hermitage (āraṇya).
"O Bhikṣus!
These four dharmas, a bodhisattva should constantly and firmly uphold for as long as life lasts; rather than losing his body and life, he shall not abandon them.
At that time, the World-Honored One further expounded this meaning, speaking in verse:
“Those of worldly wisdom should give rise to the bodhicitta;
constantly contemplate omniscience, always draw near to virtuous friends,
abide in patience and joyful aspiration, and rely upon forest hermitages.”
Like the lion king, they remain far removed from all terrors.
Those of clear wisdom who practice this Dharma can swiftly transcend the net of Māra and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
When the Blessed One had spoken this sutra, the bhikṣus and others rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Four Dharmas.
